study type: secondary analysis of a prospective cohort
exposure: cervical effacement at time of amniotomy (low effacement <=50% vs. high effacement >50%)
outcome: completion of the first stage of labor
cohort: The study included 1,256 singleton, term, nulliparous patients at a tertiary care center undergoing induction of labor and amniotomy.
finding: Low cervical effacement at the time of amniotomy, especially after cervical ripening balloon expulsion, is associated with a lower likelihood of successful induction, including reduced likelihood of completing the first stage of labor.
mod_finding: Amniotomy at low effacement was associated with a reduced likelihood of vaginal delivery.
